summary: This video demonstrates a hands-on method to diagnose play in a front lower ball joint with a dial indicator. Andy explains how to distinguish load‑carrying from non‑load‑carrying joints by spring location, then shows unloading the suspension to take weight off the joint. Using locking pliers, a gauge, a floor jack, and a pry bar, the presenter zeroes the gauge, lifts the tire for a measured vertical movement, and compares the observed play to a 0.020 inch (20 thousandths) tolerance. A movement around 0.050 inches indicates replacement is needed, while smaller movements may be acceptable depending on tolerances from the repair manual. The example uses a 2009 Chevy Suburban and ends with guidance to consult the repair manual for vehicle-specific tolerances.
title: Diagnosing a Front Lower Ball Joint Using a Dial Indicator

measuring vertical play (up-down) vs side-to-side movement
